what_this_tests: Whether the COLLAPSE of covariate-shift OOD detection generalises outside dermatology. It does NOT test the inversion.

prediction_definitions.collapse: |mean Maha AUROC on B_heldout at lambda* - 0.5| <= 0.5 * |mean Maha AUROC on B_heldout at lambda=0 - 0.5| (3-seed means)
prediction_definitions.inversion: at any dense lambda > 0, mean Maha AUROC on B_heldout lies on the opposite side of 0.5 from lambda=0, by at least 0.05

hospital_assignment.A_split: Slides 32 (smallest tumour-bearing slide, tumour frac > 0.2) and 30 (rng(42) choice among tumour-free slides 30,31,33-37) are withheld from A entirely and form the slide-disjoint ID set (19454 patches, tumour frac 0.113). The remaining 8 A slides are split patch-level, stratified by slide x label, random_state 42: 64% train / 16% checkpoint-select / 20% ID test (primary; shares slides with train).
hospital_assignment.B_split: by slide, GroupShuffleSplit test_size 0.3 random_state 42: B_adv slides [0,2,3,4,6,7,9] (38124 patches), B_heldout slides [1,5,8] (21312 patches). B labels never enter the classification loss.
hospital_assignment.C: hospital 2, all 85054 patches, never in any loss

recipe.backbone: DenseNet-121 ImageNet, BatchNorm1d on 1024-d features; classifier and GRL both on the normalised features
recipe.batches: 16 A + 16 B_adv per step (domain-balanced, as derm 50/50 ISIC/PAD)
recipe.optimiser: AdamW wd 1e-4; encoder 1e-4, domain head 1e-4 x 30, classifier 1e-4 x 0.2
recipe.grl: coef = lambda * max(0.2, 2/(1+exp(-20 p^0.5)) - 1), p = training progress
recipe.adversary_scaling_change_vs_phase12_1b: lambda multiplies the reversed gradient into the encoder only; the domain head minimises unscaled CE. Encoder gradient is identical to lambda*CE with GRL; the change removes lambda from the head's effective learning rate. Reason: in Phase 12.1b lambda in {10..300} scaled the head gradient as well (head lr x30), and the head sat at a constant uniform output with zero gradient from epoch 1.
recipe.lambda_0: coef = 0: the head still trains (online domain decodability is logged) but sends no gradient to the encoder
recipe.checkpoint: best ID accuracy on A checkpoint-select split
recipe.logging: adversary CE, adversary accuracy, mean per-sample norm of the reversed gradient at the features, and GRL coef, in 200-step windows from step 0; per-epoch adversary CE/accuracy

gates.adversary_learned: minimum over 200-step windows of mean adversary CE < 0.60. At chance from the first window onward is a null experiment.
gates.leakage_moved: post-hoc binary site probe (logistic, A ID test vs B_heldout, 70/30, 3 seeds, <=10000 per side) balanced accuracy at lambda <= lambda=0 value - 0.10
gates.id_competence: tumour accuracy on A ID test > 0.85 at lambda=0 and at every lambda in the dense set (3-seed means)
gates.detector_headroom: at lambda=0, Mahalanobis AUROC on B_heldout outside [0.45, 0.55]

dense_rule.lambda_star: smallest coarse lambda > 0 at which adversary_learned AND leakage_moved both hold
dense_rule.dense_set: {0, lambda*/sqrt(3) (3 significant digits), lambda*, next coarse lambda above lambda* if any}
dense_rule.reuse: seed-42 coarse runs are reused where the lambda coincides

stopping_rule: If ANY gate fails (adversary, leakage movement, ID competence, detector headroom), report the negative and stop. No third design, no escalation to a fourth dataset.
detectors: Mahalanobis class-conditional shared cov + 1e-3 I, cosine, kNN k=50 (30k stratified bank), MSP, Energy; statistics fit on A train only. ID reference = A ID test.
report_columns: leakage, ID balanced acc, ID ECE, OOD ECE (B_heldout), five detectors on B_heldout, hospital C Mahalanobis AUROC; per-epoch adversary logs; gate-by-gate pass/fail table

fallback_hospital_assignment.B_split: by slide, GroupShuffleSplit test_size 0.3 random_state 42: B_adv slides [20,22,23,24,26,27,29], B_heldout slides [21,25,28]

amendment_1_2026-10-09.rule: If Mahalanobis AUROC at lambda=0 on B_heldout (coarse scan, seed 42) lies inside [0.45, 0.55], the detector-headroom gate fails. That is NOT reported as a negative: switch to A=3, B=2, C=1 and rerun the coarse scan once. If the fallback also fails the headroom gate, or any gate fails under either assignment otherwise, report the negative and stop.
amendment_1_2026-10-09.reason: Hospitals 0 and 3 are both WILDS training hospitals; the A-B shift may be too small for the sweep to move (forward BCN->HAM failure mode). Hospital 2 carries the largest shift.

amendment_2_2026-10-09.slide_disjoint_id: Every ID-side number (ID accuracy, balanced accuracy, ECE, all detector AUROCs with the ID reference, site-probe leakage) is also reported with the slide-disjoint ID set (A slides 30, 32) as the ID reference, beside the patch-level ID test. Gates use the patch-level ID test (primary). Under a patch-level split no test patch is slide-disjoint, so the clean set is withheld slides rather than a subset; it is tumour-poor (11.3%), so balanced accuracy is the comparable ID metric there.

amendment_3_2026-10-09.lambda_placement_hypothesis: Phase 12.1b (and iWildCam, same codebase: train_phase15b_iwildcam.py line 142, loss = loss_cls + lambda_adv * loss_adv, GRL coefficient alpha, domain head lr x30) multiplies lambda into the domain head's own loss. Hypothesis: this, not the dataset, caused the constant-uniform adversary (CE = ln K from epoch 1).
amendment_3_2026-10-09.a_priori_caveat: Both codebases use AdamW, which is close to invariant to a constant rescaling of the loss; multiplying the head loss by lambda barely changes the head's step size. The hypothesis is therefore tested empirically, not inferred from the code.
amendment_3_2026-10-09.diagnostic: Primary assignment, seed 42, lambda in {10, 100}, placement in {loss (12.1b form), grl (Item 5 form)}, 3000 steps each, identical schedule, batches and optimiser; adversary CE, accuracy and reversed-gradient norm logged every 200 steps. No evaluation. Phase 12 is not rerun.
amendment_3_2026-10-09.confirmed_iff: for both lambda: every 200-step window of the 'loss' run has adversary CE >= 0.65 (stuck at chance, ln 2 = 0.693) AND the 'grl' run reaches a window with adversary CE < 0.60
amendment_3_2026-10-09.rejected_if: the 'loss' run reaches a window with CE < 0.60 at either lambda (placement does not reproduce the failure on this setup), or both placements stay >= 0.65 (failure independent of placement)
amendment_3_2026-10-09.if_confirmed: Report states plainly that the Camelyon17 and iWildCam failures are implementation failures, and the two limitations that attribute them to the datasets need rewriting.
